# Dual License — MIT Code, CC BY Data

**Decision.** License the repository under two licences at once: **MIT** for everything executable,
**Creative Commons Attribution 4.0** for the dataset and the written analysis. Keep the `LICENSE`
file as canonical unmodified MIT and put the split in `NOTICE`.

**Date.** 2026-07-11, [[labour-fraud-analysis]] — arrived at in the repository's final commit.

## Why

> "Code (everything under /src, /interactive, /notebooks, and the build tooling) is released under
> the MIT License; see LICENSE. The dataset and prose (everything under /data and /docs) are
> released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0); see LICENSE-DATA."
> — labour-fraud-analysis-a-forensic-data-investigation/NOTICE, 2026-07-11

The two halves of this repository are different kinds of thing. `src/` is machinery — an
anonymisation pipeline, a disclosure gate, a doc generator — that someone might reasonably lift into
their own project, where MIT's near-zero friction is the point. `data/` and `docs/` are a **citable
artefact**: a 20-table dataset and a long-form narrative, whose value is as something to reference,
and where attribution is not friction but the whole transaction. Software licences map badly onto
datasets; CC BY is built for the case.

There is a second reason specific to this repository. CC BY's attribution requirement travels with
the data, and `LICENSE-DATA` uses the space to carry the synthetic-data disclosure into any reuse:

> "IMPORTANT — SYNTHETIC DATA NOTICE"
> — labour-fraud-analysis-a-forensic-data-investigation/LICENSE-DATA, 2026-07-11

A dataset extracted from this repo and dropped into someone else's analysis arrives with a
machine-adjacent statement that every value in it is fictional. Given
[[synthesise-rather-than-redact]], that is the disclosure most likely to be lost in transit and the
one most worth attaching to the licence file. It is the same instinct as
[[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]], applied where prose usually is not.

## How it is structured

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| `LICENSE` | canonical, unmodified MIT — `/src`, `/interactive`, `/notebooks`, build tooling |
| `LICENSE-DATA` | CC BY 4.0 — `/data`, `/docs`, with the synthetic-data notice and an attribution string |
| `NOTICE` | the split itself, plus the synthetic-data statement, read first |

Keeping `LICENSE` textually canonical matters for tooling: GitHub's licence detection and every
SPDX scanner recognise unmodified MIT and fail on a hand-edited variant. The scoping lives in
`NOTICE` precisely so the licence file itself stays machine-identifiable.

## Alternatives rejected

| Option | Why not |
|---|---|
| **A single edited LICENSE carving out the data** | breaks automated licence detection; the final commit explicitly undoes this shape |
| **MIT over everything** | a software licence that says nothing useful about attributing a dataset or a narrative |
| **CC BY over everything** | discourages lifting the pipeline code, which is the reusable part |
| **No licence on the data** | default is all-rights-reserved; the dataset then cannot be cited or reused, which defeats publishing it |

The first row is the one the repository actually walked. The eighth and last commit reads
"Simplify the LICENSE to canonical MIT and note the dual license in NOTICE" — a licence file that
had been modified was restored to canonical form and the scoping moved out of it.

## Confidence and gaps

`confidence: medium`. The **arrangement** is unambiguous — three files agree and the README repeats
it. The **reasoning** above is reconstructed from what the files do; the repo states the split but
never argues for it.

**Note the tension worth holding.** The repository licenses its dataset for open reuse, while every
page about it in this wiki is `publish: false` pending clearance from the corpus holder. A permissive
licence is the author's grant over the derived artefact; it is not evidence of permission over the
source it derives from. Those are separate questions and the wiki treats them separately — see
[[labour-fraud-analysis]] and [[disclosure-gate]].
